newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia denies again to end currency board.
newsitem.headline: Estonia denies again to end currency board.

text.p: Estonia's finance ministry on Wednesday reaffirmed that the Baltic state had no intention of scrapping the currency board system under which its kroon currency is pegged at eight to one German mark.

"Neither the finance ministry, the government nor the central bank have discussed giving up the currency board principle and the pegging of the Estonian kroon to the German mark," the finance ministry said in a statement.
This was the second such statement to be issued by a government authority in a week in Estonia after a similar statement from the central bank earlier this week.
The statements came after Deutsche Bank said in a recent research note that it believed Estonia may have to abandon the currency board when Lithuania ends its currency board.
Lithuania wants to scrap the currency board, under which any rise in local currency has to be backed by a rise in foreign currency reserves.
It says the system has led to an appreciation of its currency, which is pegged at four to one dollar, and has made its exports uncompetitive.
"The government, during its session on Tuesday, expressed its firm commitment to be led by the goals set during currency reform," the Estonian finance ministry statement added.
The statement rejected any suggestion that Estonia's large trade deficit was a reason for abandoning the currency board.
Estonia has often said it has no plans to change the currency board and its effectiveness and necessity is rarely if ever questioned by politicians or financiers.
